title: My first technical interview
text:
Yesterday I had my first technical interview for a junior backend position. I prepared for a week, but I was still nervous when the call started.

The interviewer was friendly. First she asked about my previous projects, and I explained a small web app that I built for a local shop. Then we moved to the technical part. She gave me a task: write a function that finds duplicates in a list. I started to code silently, and she asked me to speak aloud. That helped a lot, because I understood my own mistake before she said anything.

There was one question I could not answer. It was about database indexes. Instead of pretending, I said, "I am not sure, but I think it makes the search faster." She smiled and explained the idea in a simple way.

At the end, I asked about the team and the tools they use. I have no answer yet, and they promised to write within a week. Whatever happens, I feel more confident now. The interview showed me what I should study next, and that is already useful.

questions.prompt: Why did the interviewer ask the author to speak aloud?
options: She could not hear the code.
It helped the author to notice his own mistake.
It was a rule of the company.
She wanted to end the interview quickly.
questions.explanation: Коли автор говорив уголос, він сам помітив свою помилку ще до підказки.

questions.prompt: What did the author do when he did not know an answer?
options: He honestly said what he thought.
He asked to change the question.
questions.explanation: Замість вдавати, що знає, він чесно сказав, що не певен, але припускає.

questions.prompt: How does the author feel at the end?
options: More confident and ready to learn
Sure that he got the job
questions.explanation: Автор каже, що почувається впевненіше й знає, що вчити далі.
